translations.text: You are our Father, ruler of all, king in glory. Therefore we call to you and ask for mercy, for you can most easily set the soul free.
You sent it long ago by your noble hand into the flesh; but where does it go now, unless you, God of angels, set it free again, the soul from its sins, by your true power?
You are the hope and comfort in the heavens, the brightest of joys; all bow down to you, the host of your spirits; with one voice they call to Christ, and all say this:
"Holy are you, holy, King of the angels of heaven, our Lord, and your judgements are right and generous; they reach to everyone, to each man according to his own deeds.
It is well for the one who does your will!"
So your high name is hallowed most gloriously in many languages, seventy-two of them, as the books say, for you, God of angels, established for every nation its custom and way of life.
They honour your work in words and deeds; by their nature they call out and praise Christ and carry forward your praise, living God, since you are made glorious throughout all the world.
Come now and have mercy, ruler of powers, and grant us your kingdom, righteous judge: the best of dwellings and eternal life, where we will find peace and love together,
Brightness of the eyes and all joy: there your holy praise is heard, and your great might, as a comfort to people, since you, God of angels, give joy to all.
Your will be done, since you, Ruler, are revealed forever throughout all the world, and you yourself are the righteous judge, the mighty counsellor, across the wide earth.
Your high throne is lofty and glorious, fair and honourable, as your Father made it, noble and eternal, where you sit at his right hand.
You are Son and Father, the one being both; so your noble nature is greatly glorified, and you help many, majesty of all kings, and you call out over all.
Your word of glory is heard far and wide when you fairly gladden your host, giving might and protection to the great army, and many thousands thank you, all the host of angels, with one voice,
just as those in the heavens, noble and eternal, ever thank you for your high majesty. Christ's pure and chosen thanes sing, and ask the true God for grace and forgiveness for all peoples;
when you grant them their request, glory-blessed King, since you are gracious to all the world.
Thanks and praise be to you for your mercy, glory and gladness; you are honoured in the kingdom of heaven, high Emperor,
and on earth, help and head of all kings, holy physician, stern and righteous, generous-hearted Lord.
You made all created things noble for yourself, and afterwards divided them into many kinds; you gave each kind its own way, and your mercy always over the children of men.
So in peace you bless our bread daily from your bounty; you rightly share out food to your people and promise them more after their departure from this life,
your Father's kingdom, which was fairly prepared in the beginning, the best of dwellings and eternal life, if we always carry out truth and right.
Give us today, Lord, your mercy and powers, and bend our mind, our thoughts and our conduct, to your will.
Establish the Holy Spirit firmly within us, in our hearts, and give us help, so that we may do your will and commit to you, glory-blessed King, our souls into your own hand.
Forgive us our sins, so that we are not ashamed afterwards, our Lord, when you sit in judgement and all people rise up who were born of woman and of man.

The decayed bones, together with the flesh, will all be made whole again; there we will afterwards clearly recognise everything we did in the kingdom of this world, better and worse; both will be ready there.
We cannot hide it at all, because the Lord knows it, and there the witnesses will be very glorious: the inhabitants of heaven, the inhabitants of earth, and thirdly the inhabitants of hell.

Then there will be terror throughout all the world, when on that day we are assigned one of two dwellings, the Lord's grace or the devil's servitude, whichever of the two we earn here in life while our powers were greatest.
But then the living God will set our souls free, just as we here forgive the poor people who have done wrong against us.

And do not let the hateful ones deceive us in temptation, or kill and burn our souls, though through our folly we have committed many sins by day and by night, idle speech and wrongful deeds, and have broken your commandments.
We now ask you, almighty God, for mercy and forgiveness; do not let your handiwork perish so shamefully, all of it, on the last day,
but deliver us from evil. We all need God's forgiveness; we have done wrong and sinned greatly.
We praise and glorify you, true God, since you, Saviour, are made known as the royal child to the living and the dead, noble and eternal above all things.
You can easily hold the whole world in one hand. Such is the glorious king.
Let it be as you yourself will, righteous judge; we all praise you, God of angels, as you are honoured forever, world without end.
